    Behind the systems

    By Way of Flint, Michigan
    Photography In black & white

    A portrait of a cybersecurity professional as an endpoint defender: vulnerability and patch management across some 1,392 endpoints in Genesee County, and the quiet, methodical work of taking identified vulnerabilities from roughly 1,050 down to 105. Security+, a B.S. in Cybersecurity from the University of Michigan–Flint, and a master's in progress.

    Read the profile ↓

    In the Work

    t Follow the work, week to week

    The work is unglamorous on purpose. Endpoints patched before they become incidents. Exceptions argued in writing, with the risk named plainly. Audit evidence gathered for HIPAA and CJIS before anyone asks for it — because the week someone asks is the wrong week to start.

    That discipline is the through-line of this portfolio: the county vulnerability count, the NULL console that refuses to show invented data, the journal that prints its corrections. Defence, done quietly, and documented like it will be read back.

    The Short Version

    Jamiah McQuiller is an IT End User Computing Technician for Genesee County, working on endpoint security, vulnerability and patch management, compliance, and risk. She holds a B.S. in Cybersecurity (minor, Computer Science) from the University of Michigan–Flint, is completing an M.S. in Cybersecurity there, and earned CompTIA Security+ in September 2026.
